== Old PC website (swccgpc.com) facts added, 24 November 2026 ==
Added 88 rows to the 2003, 2004, 2005 and 2008 tables and filled or linked 12 existing rows from posts on the old Players Committee forum (swccgpc.com, Internet Archive captures). Each new row cites the post it comes from (refs <code>pcf-TOPIC-POST</code>). Topics used: 622, 1062, 1264, 1291, 1855, 2224, 2228, 2284, 2381, 2533, 2573, 2611, 2623, 2635, 2661, 2663, 2665, 2668, 2678, 2701, 2726, 2737, 2738, 2786, 2860, 3153, 3211, 3267, 3364, 3367, 3383, 3385, 3386, 3387, 3408, 3460, 3469, 3515, 3533, 3536, 3620, 3659, 3725, 3758, 3759, 3781, 3787, 3824, 3830, 3909, 3915, 3961, 3970, 3972, 3974, 3979, 3984, 4033, 4035, 4047, 4050, 4100, 4112, 4120, 4138, 4273, 4290, 4308, 4326, 4349, 4383, 4411, 4462, 21444, 21824.

Existing rows kept as they were; only links and extra cell text were added. The [[2004 Coruscant Regionals|Coruscant Regional]], [[2005 Alderaan Regional|Alderaan Regional]] and Hoth: Ice Plains Regional rows still carry the tag "2005" at the bottom of the 2005 table. The Coruscant Regional was held on 11 December 2004, so its row could move to the 2004 table with tag 2004-12-11; the Alderaan Regional (22 January 2005) could take tag 2005-01-22. The [[2004 Mystic Visions|Mystic Visions]] row keeps tag 2004-07 although the convention ran 30 July – 1 August 2004. The [[2004 Rhode Island State Championship|Rhode Island State Championship]] row keeps "2004" and "Rhode Island" with the date and the Bridgewater, Massachusetts venue added in brackets.

=== Missing data ===
* Most local rows come from announcements only; no results were posted, so their Winner cells are blank.
* [[August 2004 Seattle tournament]]: the results post gives first names only (1st "Nick"), so the winner is not named on the List.
* [[August 2004 East Lansing tournament]]: the results post names the winner as "Matt Pietraglo [sp?]"; the spelling is not confirmed, so the winner is not named on the List.
* Hoth: Ice Plains Regional: announced for "sunday 19th of march" (2005); 19 March 2005 was a Saturday, so no date was added.
* Undated or vague items left out: a 2004 Toronto event with 14 players (1st Andrew, 2nd Pat Dinelle; date not given), monthly series in Denville (New Jersey), North Liberty (Iowa), Nashville (Tennessee) and Ambler (Pennsylvania, booster events before April 2004), weekly play days at The Evergreen State College (Olympia, cancelled 23 October 2004), an all-Decipher-games day at Dragon's Keep (Provo, 20 January 2005), a planned Lawrenceville (New Jersey) event in October 2004, a St. Peters (Missouri) event held "last sunday" before 29 September 2004, a Helm's (Pennsylvania) event the day after 23 April 2004, a San Diego event "on the 30th" (posted 30 November 2003), a T & T Toys event on 3 January 2004 that drew no players, the Franklin monthlies of November 2004 – January 2005 (not confirmed in the posts read) and the Matt Enlow Memorial Tournaments (place not stated).
* Young Jedi and Jedi Knights events (Beaverton Young Jedi tournament of 20 December 2003; Gen Con 2003 Young Jedi and Jedi Knights World Championships) are not Star Wars CCG events and were not added.
* 2004 California State Championship: a player wrote in July 2004 that it was not being held; no row added.
* The Gen Con 2003 Classic winner (Damian Loback in the gap list) is not in the topic read (t=1062), so it was not added.

=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Michigan State Championship 2004: the only source ("MI states are july 27th", noodles, 12 July 2004) gives 27 July 2004, which was a Tuesday.
* Hartford, Wisconsin tournament: posted as "October 10, Saturday"; 10 October 2004 was a Sunday. The List gives 10 October 2004.
* T & T Toys tournaments of October 2003: posted as "the 3rd" and "the 25th"; 3 October 2003 was a Friday.
* [[January 2005 College Station tournament]]: the announcement text and title say Sunday 9 January 2005; the form's date line reads 01/02/2005. The List gives 9 January 2005.
* [[February 2005 Toronto tournament]]: the announcement prints "February 13, 2004"; it was posted in January 2005 and the title says Feb. 13, so the List gives 13 February 2005.
* Game Keep tournament (3 July 2004): the post places The Game Keep in "Heritage", Tennessee (Hermitage is a Tennessee place name; the post does not say), so the List gives only "The Game Keep, Tennessee".
* Forum signatures that claim titles (Edward Fones "2004 Oregon State Champ.", band_member for 2004 Minnesota, Bryan Batdorf as 2004 Texas runner-up, "Gaurhir" for 2002 Norwegian Nationals) were not used as results. The 2004 Oregon winner comes from the event thread's results post (t=3383).

== Old PC forum (swccgpc.com) facts, wave 2, 24 November 2026 ==
Added 9 rows to the 2008 table, 20 rows to the 2006 table, and filled or linked existing rows (2008 US West Nationals, 2006 Coruscant Regional; 2005 North Dakota, Missouri, California, Oklahoma, Minnesota and Yavin IV rows; two 2004 Syracuse rows) from posts on the old Players Committee forum (Internet Archive captures). Each addition cites its post (refs <code>pcf-TOPIC-POST</code>). Topics used: 2661, 3394, 5018, 6219, 8547, 9009, 9443, 9445, 9457, 9699, 9759, 9928, 9940, 9982, 10110, 10140, 10157, 10188, 10256, 21009, 21070, 21300, 21345, 22209, 22819, 22840, 22966.

=== Missing data ===
* Tatooine Regional (2006): no date or site was posted. Results were posted on 13 June 2006 and a 14 June post calls it "last weekend", so no hub page was made.
* Yavin IV Regional (2005): Tim Simon's February 2006 recap gives the site, 26 players and Greg Shaw's unbeaten day, but no date, so no hub page was made.
* [[2006 Bespin Regional|Bespin Regional]] (April 2006) and [[2006 Tennessee DPC|Tennessee DPC]] (10 June 2006): the dates are taken from the existing hub pages, which have no forum source for them.
* Colorado, Wyoming and Massachusetts State Championships (2008): the posts of 18 August 2008 give attendance but no dates.
* Most 2006 and 2008 rows come from announcements; their Winner cells are blank because no results were posted in the captures read.

=== Left out ===
* Young Jedi events ([[2005 Young Jedi World Championship]], [[2005 Utah Young Jedi State Championship]], Glenn Hall's Beaverton Young Jedi tournaments of 27 September 2003 and 3 January 2004, and the free Young Jedi sealed event at the 2005 Oklahoma State Championship, which drew no players) were not added, following the wave 1 decision above that Young Jedi events are not Star Wars CCG events. The first two have their own pages.
* Not held or not placed: Matt Burke's NYC local of 17 June 2006 (cancelled on 31 May 2006), a Columbus, Ohio local proposed for 27 May 2006 (postponed), and the upstate New York local of 20 May 2006 (no venue stated; see [[April 2006 Syracuse tournament]]).
* Tournament directors with no List column: Kevin Elia (2005 Maryland State Championship, "as he did last year"), Jason Huffman (2005 Iowa State Championship), Joe Radi (2005 Missouri State Championship; Nick Kolnik: "I believe Joe Radi ran the show").
* 2005 Utah State Championship: Scott Church wrote that his Young Jedi event would go along with the "Star Wars States here" on 11 June at Dragon's Keep, Provo; the post does not say the Star Wars CCG event was at Dragon's Keep, so no site was added.

=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Yavin IV Regional (2005): Tim Simon's recap says [[Greg Shaw]] never lost a game and took home over $250, while the Players Committee's 2005 qualifier listing gives the two Day 2 byes to [[James Booker]] and [[Drew Scott]]. Shaw already held a Day 2 bye from the 2005 Coruscant Regional (see that row and [[2005 Coruscant Regional]]), which may explain a pass-down, but none of the posts read says so. The [[2005 East Coast Open]], announced by Tim Simon for 2 April 2005 at the same store, may or may not be the same event; none of the posts read says.
* [[2006 Yavin IV Regional]]: the hub page gives [[Reid Smith]] as 1st (from his DeckTech decklist), while Mike Carr's Worlds 2006 qualifier list (3 April 2006) gives the two Yavin IV byes to [[Steven Lewis]] and [[Justin Stratton]]; Stratton's forum signature (June 2006) links his "Yavin IV Regional Runner's Up Report". None of the posts read explains why Smith did not take a bye (for example an earlier bye). The List row gives the byes only.
* [[2008 US West Nationals]]: the existing row gives 2 August 2008; the forum board for the event reads "August 1st thru 3rd, 2008" (the weekend also held the Nevada State Championship on 1 August). The winner and runner-up are named by first name only in the source ("Kevin and Aaron"); see [[Talk:2008 US West Nationals]].
* Tierfon Regional (2006) and the 2006 Minnesota State Championship: their posts survive only in captures of neighbouring forum topics, so the topic titles are uncertain; the citations use the board name and the post's own heading.

== Players Committee forum (forum.starwarsccg.org) facts added, 24 November 2026 (wave 3) ==
Added 60 rows to the 2009, 2008, 2007 and 2006 tables and filled or linked 14 existing rows (2008 Colorado, Wyoming and Massachusetts state championships, Nevada State Championship, Dragon Con Cube Draft and Mini-Open, Dagobah Regionals, Kansas and New York state championships, Official Leagues, 2008 Match Play Championship site, 2007 Yavin 4 Regionals site, 2006 US National Championship, 2005 Yavin IV Regional) from posts on the live Players Committee forum (refs <code>sf-TOPIC-POST</code>). The posts have no Internet Archive capture yet; forum snapshots are to be added later. Topics used: 10070, 10071, 10118, 10491, 11373, 14253, 15832, 18222, 19214, 19270, 20194, 20492, 20536, 20765, 20869, 20909, 21008, 21295, 21361, 21495, 21590, 21613, 21635, 21794, 21799, 21815, 21914, 21984, 21995, 22028, 22067, 22129, 22436, 22727, 22883, 23057, 25847, 27502, 27721.
Many 2008 rows give only the Day 2 bye holder, from Cedric Simon's list of 2008 World Championship Day 2 auto bids (t22883, 29 August 2008, last edited 4 September 2008). A bye is not a win: the bye passed down when the winner already held one (for example Wyoming, where [[Brian Hunter]] won and [[Thomas McGee|Tom McGee]] took the bye).
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* 2008 Idaho State Championship: the western calendar of 17 June 2008 (t21362 p307955) planned it for Pocatello (Empire Cards/Games); the calendar post t21008 p303347, last edited 18 July 2008, gives Nampa "so that the Washington players can come". The row uses Nampa.
* 2008 Washington State Championship: t21008 p303347 gives "WA states in Auburn"; the event announcements give the Algona-Pacific Library in Pacific. The row uses Pacific.
* 2008 Colorado State Championship: the calendar gives Colorado State University; VanDriel moved it to Gryphon Games and Comics on 18 July 2008 (t21799 p316396). The row uses Gryphon.
* 2008 Dantooine Regionals: Michael Richards listed himself first (t20869 p317096), but the Day 2 bids went to Bryan Batdorf and Blake Huffman (second place per his report). The winner cell gives the byes only.
* 2008 Ralltiir Regionals (Hannover): the post names the winner only as "Angelo"; linked to [[Angelo Consoli]], who won the Norwegian Open three weeks later and, like the Hannover winner, played Profit and BHBM (t19214, t20492).
* 2005 Yavin IV Regional: Tim Simon's 2007 history post (t14253 p199507) says [[Greg Shaw]] won, with James Booker, Brad Eier and Drew Scott in the top four; the existing cell's Day 2 byes (Booker, Scott) are consistent with Shaw already holding a bye.
* 2007 European regionals: the byes are for the European Champions' MPC, not the World Championship (t15832 p216503); "Magnus Christiansen" there is linked to [[Magnus Kristiansen]].
=== Missing data ===
* Winners of most 2008 state championships whose rows give only the bye holder; sites of the Wisconsin, Kentucky, North Dakota, Florida, Georgia and Virginia 2008 events.
* Nevada Mini-Open (3 August 2008), Germany Year Ender Open and Eastern European Open: scheduled only; no results in the sources used.
=== Left out ===
* 2006 Connecticut State Championship: only a plan to run it on a Saturday (t10118 p139139); no date or site.
* 2007 World Championship venue (PasTimes, Niles): not in this wave's source posts for the List.
* "Worlds 2008 Invitational Qualifier (@ worlds 07)" bid to Justin Carulli, and the 2008 Match Play Championship bids (reviewed in September 2008): these belong on the [[2007 World Championship]] and [[2008 Match Play Championship]] pages.
* The Port Angeles Cube League bye (Jesse Reynolds, t22883 p332297): league row left as the two leagues on the official list.

== Old PC forum: left-out events re-checked, 24 November 2026 ==
The 47 events left out of the List in the earlier passes were re-checked against all forum sources, including the topics that survive on forum.starwarsccg.org.
* Added three rows from later posts in the "Tennessee tournaments" topic (t2860) that the earlier pass had not read: the Franklin tournaments of 20 November 2004 (Royce Russell, posting as Roycer, heard that 6 players came and the event was not sanctioned; p56912), 18 December 2004 (he attended and it was sanctioned; p60053) and 15 January 2005 (announcement only; p60026). This settles the "Franklin monthlies of November 2004 – January 2005" item in the left-out list above.
* Already on the List since the earlier passes: the Fallston tournament of 2 October 2004 and the [[2008 Canadian Nationals]].
* The Nashville monthly series ("every third Sat", next on 19 February 2005, posted by Micah Wooten) is the Franklin series run by the same organiser at Outer Limits; its 19 February 2005 event is [[February 2005 Franklin tournament]].
=== Still left out ===
* Matt Enlow Memorial Tournaments (3 May 2003, 25 October 2003, 17 April 2004, 11 December 2004): the results post (t4248 p58346) still gives no place.
* SWCCG Classic tournament at T & T Toys, Duluth, in February 2004: a post of 5 February 2004 (t2224 p40240) says "this weekend", but no day is given.
* Columbus (Ohio) local planned for 27 May 2006: postponed by the organiser (t9488 p136681 / t9699); no later date found.
* All other items in the left-out lists above: no new source gives a date and place.

== PC Discord and Retro Club facts added, 24 November 2026 ==
Added rows for KublaCon (25 May 2024), the Oceanside retro tournament (20 July 2024) and Talaga Nights (6–8 April 2025). None of the sources gives a winner for these events, so the Winner cells are blank. The Oceanside thread title says Vista; the organizer's update in the same thread moved the event to Black Plague Brewing in Oceanside.
=== Missing data ===
* Left out: the "2026 Retro Jawa Championship" announced on Discord on 20 March 2026 with the format "Premiere - Death Star II (Jawa)" (Bill in #retro-league-pc, SWCCG Players Committee Discord (20 March 2026), [https://discord.com/channels/401469156907679746/1190452472477655170/1484639872353571070 Discord message]). The forum names the same event, announced the same day, the 2026 Retro Ewok Championship (see [[Ewok]]); its dates and results are not on the wiki yet.

=== Possibly faulty data ===
* A Discord list of fall 2023 events gives "Oct 7-8 Carmel, IN" (Solidsnack3 in #cantina, SWCCG Players Committee Discord (25 September 2023), [https://discord.com/channels/401469156907679746/401469157587025922/1155856747332915231 Discord message]); [[2023 Regional Championships]] gives the Nal Hutta Regionals as 7 October 2023 in Indianapolis, Indiana.
